cheat_sheet.title: Text Processing, Tokens and Numerical Representation — Structural Cheat Sheet
cheat_sheet.introduction: This sheet turns Text Processing, Tokens and Numerical Representation into visible relationships. It is a reference for planning, tracing, debugging, and explaining—not a list to memorize.
cheat_sheet.why_it_matters: The level contributes directly to a evaluated and safety-bounded NLP application. Each concept helps the learner move from an ambiguous task to a contract, a representation, a verified transition, and an explainable result.

mental_model.summary: Represent the work as tokens, vectors, weighted relationships, retrieval records, and evaluation sets before translating it into implementation details.
reasoning_cycle: Model variables, state, constraints, and relationships

core_concepts.title: Text units, Unicode, and normalization
core_concepts.rule: Text is encoded as Unicode sequences; normalization choices can merge visually equivalent forms while case and punctuation may carry meaning.

core_concepts.title: Tokenization and vocabulary boundaries
core_concepts.rule: A tokenizer maps text to token IDs under a fixed vocabulary, and different segmentations change sequence length and information sharing.

core_concepts.title: Bag-of-words vectors
core_concepts.rule: A bag-of-words vector records token counts or presence while discarding order, producing a sparse document-feature matrix.

core_concepts.title: TF-IDF weighting
core_concepts.rule: TF-IDF raises terms frequent in one document but rare across the collection, with smoothing and normalization affecting scale.

core_concepts.title: N-grams and local order
core_concepts.rule: Word or character n-grams retain bounded local order at the cost of a much larger feature space.

core_concepts.title: Text cleaning without destroying signal
core_concepts.rule: Every cleaning step encodes an assumption; validate whether punctuation, casing, numbers, dialect, or spelling are useful for the task.

core_concepts.title: Sequence padding, masks, and lengths
core_concepts.rule: Batches align variable sequences using padding, while masks ensure padded positions do not affect computation or evaluation.

core_concepts.title: Text data pipelines and leakage
core_concepts.rule: Split by the real deployment unit before fitting vocabulary or statistics, and track source, consent, duplicates, and labels.

common_mistakes: Starting with syntax before defining the input-output contract.
Combining current state and a candidate update so rejection cannot be safe.
Treating an observed normal result as proof for every boundary.
Choosing a structure because it is familiar rather than because its operations match the constraints.
Ignoring empty, missing, duplicate, maximum-size, repeated, or out-of-order cases.
Hiding failures instead of representing loading, empty, rejected, and error states explicitly.
Optimizing before measuring the actual bottleneck or risk.
Explaining what the implementation does without explaining why its invariant proves correctness.
debugging_checklist: Can I restate the exact expected output?

Is the boundary inclusive or exclusive?
Can an invalid or repeated event mutate valid state?
Are asynchronous or external results stale, missing, or out of order?
Does the representation match the operation mix and constraints?
Did the repair pass the original failure and nearby regression cases?

lessons.title: Text units, Unicode, and normalization
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Text units, Unicode, and normalization within a bounded language-assistance system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Text units, Unicode, and normalization to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Text units, Unicode, and normalization is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Text is encoded as Unicode sequences; normalization choices can merge visually equivalent forms while case and punctuation may carry meaning.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Text units, Unicode, and normalization, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use tokens, vectors, weighted relationships, retrieval records, and evaluation sets. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Text units, Unicode, and normalization
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Text is encoded as Unicode sequences; normalization choices can merge visually equivalent forms while case and punctuation may carry meaning.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Text units, Unicode, and normalization.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

reasoning: Write the inclusive or exclusive boundary symbolically.
Evaluate the predicate before changing state.
Apply the same rule used for ordinary valid input.
Verify that the output remains representable and accessible.

worked_examples.scenario: An input violates one required relationship or arrives in an unsupported state.
worked_examples.input: An out-of-contract value paired with a previously valid state.
reasoning: Identify the failed constraint and stop before commit.
Keep the previous valid state unchanged.
Return a specific, non-sensitive explanation or recovery path.
Record the case as evidence for a regression check.
worked_examples.output: A controlled rejection, preserved prior state, and actionable feedback.

common_mistakes: Beginning implementation before defining the required output.
Changing state before the input or transition has been validated.
Memorizing the label 'Text units, Unicode, and normalization' without applying its governing relationship.
Testing only one convenient normal case and assuming boundaries behave identically.
edge_cases: The smallest valid input or empty valid structure, when allowed.
The largest documented input, count, depth, size, or duration.
A duplicate, repeated event, retry, or already-completed transition.
Malformed, missing, stale, unauthorized, or otherwise out-of-contract input.
debugging_strategy: Freeze the first input that produces a wrong observable result.
Write the expected trace beside the observed trace.
Locate the first row where state, constraint, or output diverges.
Repair the rule or boundary responsible for that first divergence.
Rerun the failing case plus one normal, one boundary, and one rejection case.

project.title: Text Processing, Tokens and Numerical Representation: Evaluated And Safety-Bounded Nlp Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a bounded language-assistance system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate evaluated and safety-bounded NLP application that demonstrates all eight skills from Text Processing, Tokens and Numerical Representation. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Text is encoded as Unicode sequences; normalization choices can merge visually equivalent forms while case and punctuation may carry meaning.
A tokenizer maps text to token IDs under a fixed vocabulary, and different segmentations change sequence length and information sharing.
A bag-of-words vector records token counts or presence while discarding order, producing a sparse document-feature matrix.
TF-IDF raises terms frequent in one document but rare across the collection, with smoothing and normalization affecting scale.
Word or character n-grams retain bounded local order at the cost of a much larger feature space.
Every cleaning step encodes an assumption; validate whether punctuation, casing, numbers, dialect, or spelling are useful for the task.
Batches align variable sequences using padding, while masks ensure padded positions do not affect computation or evaluation.
Split by the real deployment unit before fitting vocabulary or statistics, and track source, consent, duplicates, and labels.

first divergence, repair, trade-off, and next iteration

Submission evidence cannot be reproduced.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Evaluation sets and error analysis is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Stratify errors by class, language form, length, ambiguity, and subgroup to turn metric gaps into model or data actions.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Evaluation sets and error analysis, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Text Classification, Embeddings and Similarity: Evaluated And Safety-Bounded Nlp Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a bounded language-assistance system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate evaluated and safety-bounded NLP application that demonstrates all eight skills from Text Classification, Embeddings and Similarity. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Define allowed inputs, label meaning, multi-class or multi-label structure, uncertainty, and the operational action triggered by a prediction.
Linear classifiers weight token features, creating a transparent baseline that often performs strongly on limited labeled data.
An embedding maps an item to a dense vector where distance or angle is intended to reflect selected relationships.
Cosine similarity compares vector direction rather than magnitude, but meaningful interpretation still depends on how the embeddings were trained.
Embed a query and candidates under the same model, retrieve nearby vectors, then validate relevance with task-specific labels.
Imbalanced labels require per-class metrics, suitable sampling or weighting, and thresholds tied to error costs.
Vector neighborhoods can reproduce training associations and underrepresent languages, dialects, or domains.
Stratify errors by class, language form, length, ambiguity, and subgroup to turn metric gaps into model or data actions.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Attention as weighted aggregation is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Attention computes query-key compatibility, normalizes weights, and returns a weighted sum of value vectors.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Attention as weighted aggregation, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Transformer blocks and residual paths is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Attention and feed-forward transformations are wrapped with residual connections and normalization to preserve information and trainability.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Transformer blocks and residual paths, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Sequence Models, Attention and Transformers: Evaluated And Safety-Bounded Nlp Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a bounded language-assistance system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate evaluated and safety-bounded NLP application that demonstrates all eight skills from Sequence Models, Attention and Transformers. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: A recurrent model updates a hidden state from the current token and previous state, compressing prefix information through time.
Long sequences create repeated transformations that can weaken or amplify gradients and overload a fixed hidden state.
Attention computes query-key compatibility, normalizes weights, and returns a weighted sum of value vectors.
Each sequence position produces queries, keys, and values; pairwise scores create a sequence-by-sequence relationship matrix.
Because attention alone is insensitive to token order, positional features inject absolute or relative sequence relationships.
Attention and feed-forward transformations are wrapped with residual connections and normalization to preserve information and trainability.
A causal mask blocks future positions, while a padding mask blocks artificial batch padding; they encode different constraints.
Pretraining learns broad statistical representations; adaptation changes task behavior but does not guarantee truth, fairness, or domain coverage.

constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.
Do not hide invalid input, unavailable data, or failure behind a successful-looking state.
Keep current valid state recoverable until a candidate transition passes validation.
Do not embed secrets, real credentials, personal data, or private endpoints.
Make all important output and error states accessible and testable.
Record assumptions and unsupported cases explicitly.
The submitted result must be reproducible from the included instructions.

The diagram disagrees with the implemented flow.

lessons.title: Prompt contracts and bounded tasks
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Prompt contracts and bounded tasks within a bounded language-assistance system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Prompt contracts and bounded tasks to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Prompt contracts and bounded tasks is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. A reliable prompt states role, input boundaries, required output schema, uncertainty behavior, and prohibited actions.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Prompt contracts and bounded tasks, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use tokens, vectors, weighted relationships, retrieval records, and evaluation sets. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

lessons.title: Structured output and schema validation
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Structured output and schema validation within a bounded language-assistance system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Structured output and schema validation to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Structured output and schema validation is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Generated text becomes application data only after parsing, schema validation, and safe handling of missing or extra fields.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Structured output and schema validation, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use tokens, vectors, weighted relationships, retrieval records, and evaluation sets. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Structured output and schema validation
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Grounding and citation verification is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. A grounded answer must be supported by retrieved evidence, and citation checks must verify that the cited passage entails the claim.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Grounding and citation verification, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

lessons.title: Failure modes and resilient application design
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Failure modes and resilient application design within a bounded language-assistance system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Failure modes and resilient application design to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Failure modes and resilient application design is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Handle hallucination, prompt injection, missing evidence, latency, refusal, tool error, and partial output as explicit states.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Failure modes and resilient application design, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use tokens, vectors, weighted relationships, retrieval records, and evaluation sets. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Failure modes and resilient application design
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Handle hallucination, prompt injection, missing evidence, latency, refusal, tool error, and partial output as explicit states.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.

project.title: LLM Applications, Retrieval and Structured Generation: Evaluated And Safety-Bounded Nlp Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a bounded language-assistance system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate evaluated and safety-bounded NLP application that demonstrates all eight skills from LLM Applications, Retrieval and Structured Generation. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: A reliable prompt states role, input boundaries, required output schema, uncertainty behavior, and prohibited actions.
Generated text becomes application data only after parsing, schema validation, and safe handling of missing or extra fields.
A retrieval system chunks approved sources, indexes representations, retrieves candidates, and supplies traceable context for generation.
Chunk boundaries trade completeness against specificity, while reranking and token budgets determine which evidence reaches the model.
A grounded answer must be supported by retrieved evidence, and citation checks must verify that the cited passage entails the claim.
Treat model-proposed actions as untrusted plans; validate arguments, permissions, target identity, side effects, and confirmation needs.
Store only purposeful, consented facts with provenance, lifetime, user controls, and separation between instructions and retrieved content.
Handle hallucination, prompt injection, missing evidence, latency, refusal, tool error, and partial output as explicit states.

structural_patterns.name: Bias and multilingual evaluation

structural_patterns.rule: Evaluate dialects, languages, identities, and culturally dependent meanings with appropriate reviewers and sample-size uncertainty.

structural_patterns.name: Privacy and sensitive-data controls
structural_patterns.when_to_use: When the task depends on privacy and sensitive data controls.
structural_patterns.rule: Minimize collection, detect and redact sensitive data, constrain retention, isolate access, and test memorization or disclosure risks.

structural_patterns.name: Production monitoring and change control
structural_patterns.when_to_use: When the task depends on production monitoring and change control.
structural_patterns.rule: Track quality, safety, latency, cost, retrieval health, model versions, and prompt versions with staged changes and rollback.

structural_patterns.name: Responsible launch and incident response
structural_patterns.when_to_use: When the task depends on responsible launch and incident response.
structural_patterns.rule: Launch only with owners, user disclosure, feedback and appeal paths, escalation, containment, recovery, and documented limitations.

lessons.title: Task-specific evaluation design
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Task-specific evaluation design within a bounded language-assistance system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Task-specific evaluation design to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Task-specific evaluation design is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Define representative inputs, reference criteria, scoring rules, slices, and acceptance thresholds before optimizing a language system.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Task-specific evaluation design, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use tokens, vectors, weighted relationships, retrieval records, and evaluation sets. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Safety threat models and red teaming is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Safety threat models and red teaming, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

lessons.title: Production monitoring and change control
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Production monitoring and change control within a bounded language-assistance system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Production monitoring and change control to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Production monitoring and change control is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Track quality, safety, latency, cost, retrieval health, model versions, and prompt versions with staged changes and rollback.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Production monitoring and change control, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use tokens, vectors, weighted relationships, retrieval records, and evaluation sets. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Production monitoring and change control
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Track quality, safety, latency, cost, retrieval health, model versions, and prompt versions with staged changes and rollback.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.

Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Production monitoring and change control.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.

Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

reasoning: Write the inclusive or exclusive boundary symbolically.
Evaluate the predicate before changing state.

reasoning: Identify the failed constraint and stop before commit.
Keep the previous valid state unchanged.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship

Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Responsible launch and incident response, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Evaluation, Safety, Bias and Production NLP Systems: Evaluated And Safety-Bounded Nlp Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a bounded language-assistance system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate evaluated and safety-bounded NLP application that demonstrates all eight skills from Evaluation, Safety, Bias and Production NLP Systems. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

test evidence
decision record

Identify users, assets, misuse cases, failure severity, safeguards, and residual risk; test only in authorized controlled environments.
Evaluate dialects, languages, identities, and culturally dependent meanings with appropriate reviewers and sample-size uncertainty.
